stories.title: S&P 500 sales growth hits its highest level in nearly five years
stories.summary: S&P 500 companies are growing sales at the fastest pace in almost five years, according to MarketWatch, a trend CNBC's markets desk flags as one of the two big things traders are watching this week. The pickup in top-line growth is drawing attention as investors weigh how durable corporate revenue strength is heading into the back half of the year.
stories.whyItMatters: Revenue growth, not just margin expansion, is a cleaner signal of underlying economic demand, so a multi-year high matters for how investors price stocks from here.
whatToWatch: Whether upcoming earnings reports confirm broad-based sales strength or a narrower set of drivers
How this week's trading responds to the two factors CNBC says it's watching
questions: Is the sales growth broad-based across sectors or concentrated in a few industries?

stories.title: Stocks beating the S&P 500 hit a 4-year high — and MarketWatch says more could join
stories.summary: The number of individual stocks outperforming the S&P 500 is at its highest level in four years, MarketWatch reports, and the outlet argues that figure should climb further from here. The trend points to a broadening of market gains beyond the index's largest constituents.
stories.whyItMatters: A widening group of outperformers signals healthier market breadth, which investors watch as a check on whether rallies are being carried by just a handful of mega-cap names.
whatToWatch: Whether breadth continues to widen in coming weeks
How mega-cap concentration in the index evolves relative to the broader stock count
questions: What specifically is driving MarketWatch's expectation that the number rises further?
